conclusion: The smoke test requires a year slider during reveal, but the component intentionally removes it. This known-false condition is sufficient to trigger the generic reveal failure. The saved year reveal itself matches the intended UI.
answeringScreenshot: The question asks when bounty runes first spawned. The year readout is 2017, with a slider and Lock control.
revealScreenshot: The board shows Correct year, 2014 and Your answer: 2017. The result panel shows Incorrect, the explanation and zero gold. The crowd split lists the submitted and correct years. No slider is visible.
expectedBehavior: The existing component renders the slider only when hasRange and phase is not reveal. Reveal uses a correct-year readout and separate submitted-year text.
comparison: The prior accepted wrong-answer screenshot for the TI first-year question uses the same correct-year label/readout and submitted-year layout without a slider.
recommendedAssertion: Verify the reveal board phase, correct-year data and label, matching correct-year readout, submitted-year text, and slider absence. Keep the report-layout check and record both pre-open and post-open bounds plus the comparison result.
limits: This finding identifies a sufficient failing subcondition, not every possible cause of the generic assertion.
The saved output omits pre-open report-panel bounds. The no-shift condition cannot be verified from the saved screenshots or reported final bounds.
This is read-only screenshot and source inspection. No edits, new browser sessions, app runs or data changes were performed.
